name: COB — VCB.1 — stale other-carrier EOB with Our Insurance primary
description: Ten steps mapping onto the VCB.1 source document: identify the PX_VCB event, establish the EOB is not a prior transaction of a processed claim, confirm from the Limited Liability record that Our Insurance is primary, match the EOB on the COB sub-tab against the carrier that record lists, delete the CB - Commercial popup through the Actions menu, then validate the claim with that information off it and pay it.

steps.name: Review all events and identify the VCB event
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. Review every event set on the claim, informational ones included, before paying, denying or routing it — that review is what the established hierarchy asks for when more than one event is set. PX_VCB is the hard edit you are resolving: it fires because the claim still carries information from another insurer while the updated Limited Liability record shows Our Insurance as primary, so that other insurer's information is no longer needed. Read the rest of the list to check whether any event must be resolved before PX_VCB. If one is present, resolve it first; if none is, proceed. The two events beside it are informational, so nothing of higher priority is present and you proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Event Resolution tab is opened while this step is active. Visits only fire on a user click, so the trainee opens it deliberately.
steps.hint: On 'Event Resolution', All Edits lists PX_VCB as the hard edit with two informational events beside it. Nothing of higher priority is listed, so no event blocks the review.
steps.checklistItem: Review all events and identify the VCB event

steps.name: Search history for a claim matching this one
steps.description: Before acting on the other insurer's EOB, establish whether it is a prior transaction of a claim that has already been processed. Open the Search tab and its Claims sub-tab — the system has already filled the criteria with the subscriber, the service-from date and the provider tax ID — and click Search. If a history claim matching this claim comes back, the EOB is a prior transaction of a processed claim and the alternate guidelines apply; if none does, proceed. The only claim returned is this claim itself, so no history claim matches it and you proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes on the Search press. The results stay off screen until then, so the answer is produced by the trainee rather than read on arrival.
steps.hint: On 'Search → Claims', click the Search button. Compare the DCN on the row that comes back with the DCN of the claim you are working.
steps.checklistItem: Search history for a claim matching this one

steps.name: Review the Limited Liability record
steps.description: Review the Limited Liability record for the details of the reason Our Insurance is the primary carrier. Open the Search tab and its Limited Liability sub-tab; the record is already on screen for this member. Our Insurance may be primary for any of several reasons — an individual with no coordination of benefits, both our plan and an individual plan being primary, the other carrier being an Individual plan, the other plan being one Our Health does not coordinate with, the Birthday Rule, a court order for coverage of dependents, or the member being the spouse under another plan. The record reads Type COB, effective 01/01/2024 with no end date, and Order of benefits 'P – Our Insurance is primary', so an LL record is available and Our Insurance is the primary carrier. You proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Limited Liability sub-tab is opened while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Search → Limited Liability', read the record's Type, Effective date, End date and Order of benefits, then open it for the policy details.

steps.name: Verify the EOB against the LL record
steps.description: Determine whether the EOB on the claim is from the carrier the Limited Liability record lists as secondary. Open the Claim Data tab and its COB sub-tab, where the other insurer's EOB is listed with its name, policy and EOB date above the allowed, coinsurance, discount and paid amounts. Compare the policy on that EOB with the policy on the LL record. If the EOB is from the carrier listed as secondary, the COB popup is to be deleted; if it is from some other carrier, it stays. The EOB is from the Individual policy listed in the LL record, so the popup must be deleted and you proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Data → COB sub-tab is opened while this step is active.
steps.hint: On 'Claim Data → COB', read the Policy ID on the Commercial panel and check it against the Policy # on the Limited Liability record.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the EOB against the LL record

steps.name: Open the Delete Popup action
steps.description: The EOB is from the carrier the LL record lists, so the COB popup is no longer needed and comes off the claim. Open the Actions menu on the claim and select Delete Popup from the available options. The menu carries several other options; Delete Popup is the one this procedure uses. The popup selection window is then displayed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Delete Popup panel is opened. The press is refused, and the dialog stays shut, until this step is active.
steps.hint: Open the 'Action menu' on the claim summary bar and choose 'Delete Popup'. The other options in the menu are not used by this procedure.

steps.name: Select the CB-Commercial popup
steps.description: In the 'Please select the popup to delete' dropdown, select CB-Commercial — the popup carrying the other insurer's EOB you just reviewed on the COB sub-tab.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the dropdown is set to CB-Commercial while this step is active.
steps.hint: In the Delete Popup window, open the 'Please select the popup to delete' dropdown and choose CB-Commercial.

steps.name: Submit the deletion request
steps.description: Click the Submit button on the popup window to submit the deletion request. Submit does not delete anything by itself — it asks you to confirm, and it is refused while no popup is selected.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when Submit is pressed with CB-Commercial selected. A Submit with nothing selected is refused, writes the retry message and completes nothing.
steps.hint: Click 'Submit' in the Delete Popup window. If nothing happens, check that CB-Commercial is selected in the dropdown.

steps.name: Confirm the popup deletion
steps.description: A confirmation popup is displayed asking you to confirm deletion of the CB popup. Select Yes to confirm. Once confirmed, the data under the COB sub-tab is erased and processing continues in accordance with all current established unit guidelines. Selecting No instead leaves the popup, and the EOB under it, exactly where they are.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes on Yes. No completes nothing and returns the dialog to the selection, with the COB data intact.
steps.hint: In the 'Confirm Delete Popup' window, click 'Yes'. Reopen 'Claim Data → COB' afterwards and the Commercial panel is gone.

steps.name: Validate the claim
steps.description: The other insurer's information is off the claim, so run the claim through validation before deciding anything. Click Validate on the claim summary bar. The claim is processed again without the COB popup, and the Validation section on the Event Resolution tab reports what came back — read it and confirm nothing is left outstanding. Validate is held back until the deletion is confirmed, so what it reports describes the claim as it now stands rather than as it arrived.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when Validate is pressed while this step is active. Validate carries no guard of its own — the step order is what holds it back until the popup has been deleted.
steps.hint: Click 'Validate' on the claim summary bar, then read the System message under 'Event Resolution → Validation'.

steps.name: Submit the Pay decision
steps.description: The COB popup has been deleted and all current established unit guidelines have been followed, so the claim can be processed. Select Pay from the Decision dropdown on the claim summary and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the claim is submitted with Pay. Deny or Pend does not complete it.
steps.hint: Choose 'Pay' from the Decision dropdown on the claim summary bar and click Submit.
